name: takeaway text
text: Persistent lab state supports continuity. It does not solve continual learning in model weights.

Slide 1. Goal comes before topology. The lab operating model supports long-running independent research and safe local evolution. Improvements remain candidates until checked. Contributions to central AI4R and upstream OpenJiuwen are separate. Intended benefits require measurement.
Quote exactly from Andrej Karpathy at 00:00:07–00:01:44 in the publisher transcript, https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/andrej-karpathy . The quote motivates external continuity; we do not claim that saving project state solves his wider continual-learning concern. No endorsement is implied. The research brief supplies objectives and limits, not a one-pass task script.

Core deployment view. Each lab runs a complete independently versioned AI4R with its own research, factory and RSI. JiuwenSwarm provides native skills, tools/MCP, teams/workflows and evolution integration points; do not create a competing generic skill manager. CC is our deployable capability package/contract, not a claim that upstream Skills are OCI images. Use native skill discovery/invocation and scoped visibility, with thin adapters to pinned CC containers. Domain applications may be long-lived CC services and retain application state. The stable supervisor is an execution-control responsibility: reuse JiuwenBox where compatible, Docker for OCI ownership, and provider APIs for whole-VM stop. Model routing is available to both AI4R and container CCs. General/domain sources have different storage backends and feed selected versions into a lab. Lab-local factory output and upstream contributions are detailed on slide 5. No central research runtime controls every lab.

name: subtitle

name: source

name: takeaway text
text: Continue until supported completion, a real blocker, a human pause or the resource limit.

Slide 4. This is a recurrent research process, not a list of singular tasks completed once in order. Goals persist across sessions. Local specialists can retry, repair and adjust methods within their assignment. Material discoveries, requirements changes, failed prerequisites or no progress can revise strategy. Only justified near-term work gets dispatched; many independent ready jobs may overlap. A failed attempt is retained rather than relabeled success. Accepted negative/inconclusive science can advance research. Strong checking and bounded cumulative spending remain in the loop. User permissions stay authoritative. A human changes scope/completion criteria; producer suggestions do not rewrite them. New capabilities become options for future work. Persistent state supports restarting the cycle without reconstructing it from chat.

name: takeaway text
text: Factory CCs create or upgrade other CCs. New versions enter future work after independent qualification.

The CC Factory is a logical workflow/bundle composed from capability capsules, not an intrinsically separate kind of runtime or a mandatory standalone service. Illustrative roles are ingest/analyze, build/test and package; these are not a fixed count or separate mandatory containers. The lab research workflow also composes CCs. A factory bundle may be exposed as one composite CC with a stable interface, versioned composition and pinned dependencies, while its constituent CCs remain independently usable. Bundle/group by purpose; deploy separate processes only for isolation, dependency or resource needs. A lab contains these bundles plus durable state, native JiuwenSwarm orchestration and execution infrastructure. Do not equate a whole VM or supervisor with an ordinary generated CC.
Factory components use the same lab CC library, model routes, execution controller, permissions, budgets and persistent storage as research components. They can reuse ingestion, analysis, testing and other general tools instead of duplicating them. Checkers may themselves be CCs, but qualification authority, fixed acceptance criteria and permission to admit/promote a candidate remain independently assigned. A producer cannot rewrite its own acceptance rules. A factory can propose upgrades to its own constituent CCs; active versions remain pinned and recovery/control stays stable until separately qualified replacement. No uncontrolled recursive self-upgrade is implied.
General mother-AI4R packages, domain collections and lab-generated packages retain different source/image storage. User/AI needs, data/repos/papers, mental models/methods and repeated/critical planning gaps can initiate creation or upgrade. Mental-model Skills offer source-inspired methods; evaluation is needed before claiming person fidelity or decision improvements. Functional verification covers the declared task and compatibility; specialist superiority requires a matched comparison. Local qualification permits local future use, while mother-AI4R release adoption and generic upstream JiuwenSwarm contribution remain separate reviewed paths.
JiuwenSwarm Skill/tool/MCP and team/workflow interfaces are the intended composition surface; factory bundles should use these rather than introduce another generic manager. Slide 6. Both AI4R and containerized CCs may invoke shared inference through a stable lab-scoped model interface. At launch inject the reachable base URL or client configuration, scoped credential reference, and authorized model aliases; container localhost is not the guest host. Authors declare roles and required features such as tool calling, structured output, modality and context capacity, with an optional exact model/version constraint. The lab operator or authorized configuration fills the available-model registry and route mappings. Availability alone is not compatibility. Resolve the binding before invocation, record the selected model/version/route and inference settings, and preserve it for the attempt. Endpoint relocation can preserve a model binding; replacing the model requires explicit compatible policy/new binding, and exact-model experiments cannot silently switch. Missing compatible routes wait or fail visibly.
This is a logical responsibility, not a requirement for another custom daemon. Prefer existing model adapters and injected configuration initially; evaluate a gateway if centralized credential/routing policy justifies it. JiuwenBox documents inference request routing and API-key injection; LiteLLM documents public model names mapped to provider deployments. Neither establishes our full contract. Provider secrets stay out of images, and scoped access applies at the serving/gateway boundary. A private model appears only in its own lab routes, never in another lab or the shared service catalogue. Shared serving remains external and survives a lab stop.

name: takeaway text
text: Reserve scarce compute for training. A private model does not become a shared endpoint automatically.

Slide 7. This is a private model workload, not a change to the default shared-inference service. Fine-tuning can mutate lab-owned weight/checkpoint copies. No other sandbox may call the private endpoint or read its weights/checkpoints. Enforce lab-scoped network policy, bind addresses and authorization, not only a hostname convention. Do not register it with shared gateways or service discovery. Operator administration and explicit export are distinct from sandbox access. Any future sharing requires a separate explicit promotion decision; nothing automatically opens cross-lab access. A private experiment can still use authorized shared inference as an external tool, but that shared endpoint is not its private model.
The lab needs an allocated compute/device route. VM ownership alone does not give it a GPU. If the selected VM provider cannot expose the required accelerator, mark that profile unavailable until a separately qualified lab-exclusive execution binding is designed. Do not claim Spark guest GPU passthrough. Memory, storage, checkpoint staging and GPU reservations count against real capacity. Training jobs may need exclusivity to protect other labs and valid comparisons. No new training framework is selected by this diagram.

name: takeaway text
text: The stop path must remain usable when the agent hangs. Unknown external effects need reconciliation.

Slide 8. Pause stops dispatch; it does not mean compute is released. Supervisor cancellation requests termination, escalates within a configured bound, then verifies process/job status. Normal lab stop quiesces/cancels owned work, stops local services and preserves project data. Independent host/provider control can force-stop the VM if guest control hangs. Force power-off is not an application-consistent checkpoint. Reconcile incomplete work at restart; do not silently replay external effects. Separate explicit deletion decides data disposition. TTL/idle policies may not delete unique project state.
Persistent volume placement, independent backup destination and restoration are concrete deployment inputs. Backup consistency and old-writer fencing are necessary. A copied simulator volume does not recreate live physics state unless the application supports it. Shared inference remains available when one lab stops. Human guest administration may override protections; no claim of tamper-proof evidence against the lab owner.
https://libvirt.org/manpages/virsh.html ; shutdown and destroy/power-off are distinct from storage deletion. Provider support must be qualified.

title: The stack follows the lab’s responsibilities

name: title
text: The stack follows the lab’s responsibilities

name: subtitle
text: Reuse compatible components and keep AI4R’s research and qualification decisions under our control

name: source
text: Selected direction with explicit qualifications. No platform installation or integrated runtime validation is claimed.

name: takeaway text
text: First proof: continue a research cycle, reuse a CC, stop a runaway job and recover its retained project.

Slide 9. The stack is concrete at the responsibility/interface level. Exact host/provider, image pins, GPU allocation and model server are deployment qualifications, not fabricated current installations. Reuse OpenJiuwen where it preserves our contracts. JiuwenBox handles compatible sandbox/tool operations and may inform lifecycle adapters; it is not the whole VM manager or generic OCI engine. Existing native interfaces guide compatibility tests. Keep AI4R-specific packages, artifact transfer, independent qualification and research revisions under our ownership. Coder is an optional later workspace-access evaluation, not the selected research control plane.
First demonstrator has recurring research with at least one material revision, concurrent independent work where supported, a package import/qualification/invocation, shared endpoint requests with per-lab limits, private model access denial from another lab, actual job stop and independent VM stop, then retained-state continuation. Controlled drivers are distinguished from autonomous decisions. Measure useful outcomes, restart cost, total model/checking cost, resources and isolation failures. No benchmark gain is assumed.

name: takeaway text
text: A Skill is guidance and assets. A CC adds the packaged implementation and research execution contract.

Compare with the preceding original OpenJiuwen system figure: composition, shared execution and feedback remain the common structure. Here the integration mapping is concrete. providers/skills.py exposes a single physical library with member/team visibility metadata; installation does not by itself grant member access. providers/tools.py supplies config-based tools; docs/en/MCPConfiguration.md supports stdio, SSE and streamable HTTP tool services. providers/evolution_rails.py wraps native TeamSkillCreateRail / TeamSkillEvolutionRail / SkillEvolutionRail rather than creating another generic evolution system. SkillManager handles installation/library and marketplace operations. These mechanisms are reuse candidates, not proof of OCI packaging, independent research validity or sandbox lifecycle guarantees.
Our CC factory should emit compatible native skill/tool assets and packaged implementations; qualification and pinned invocation metadata sit around these extension points. Keep task-level tests, durable artifact transfer and whole-lab lifecycle under AI4R contracts. Do not indiscriminately enable currently disabled M1 planner flags; this is a bounded M2 adapter migration. Generic bug fixes, integration hooks and reusable methods can be proposed to JiuwenSwarm with reproducible tests. Lab-specific capsules can remain private or go through mother AI4R release review.

name: subtitle

name: source
text: Proposed checks. None is marked passed by this presentation or by the existence of these diagrams.

Failure scenarios include unavailable endpoint with no silent model substitution, missing GPU route, exhausted disk, corrupt backup, missing accepted input, failed qualification, stale plan revision and process interruption. A visible blocker or supported scientific negative can be valid. Protected acceptance and budget exits are not bypassed by the research loop. Runtime demonstrations must name exact versions, configurations and observed outcomes. Short trials establish bounded feasibility, not general day-long autonomy or scientific correctness.

name: takeaway text
text: Shared services address limited capacity. They do not remove the need for admission, quotas and measurement.

Decision ledger. Default endpoint sharing does not expose lab-private models or research state. Co-location is optional. Coder is an access/provisioning comparison rather than the chosen research architecture. GPU VM passthrough is not assumed; private accelerator use requires a supported binding. The original shared-host-container alternative remains in Designs/Lab Design Comparison.md; the user retained VM per lab and selected its visual style.

preview: Our need | JiuwenBox provides | Integration / remaining responsibility

text:
Direct source inspection at upstream 02b37f47fbefe80a58e4ed88606120818ca44ac3, October 27, 2026. README.md; src/jiuwenbox/server/sandbox_manager.py; server/runtime/process.py; proxy/inference_privacy_proxy.py; policy/cgroup controls.
The proxy uses path-prefix route targets and injected credentials; this is not evidence of model-feature discovery, alias-to-model matching or experiment pinning. Existing routes may serve container clients if their authorized network path is configured. No automatic CC container connectivity is assumed.
Sandbox stop calls runtime.stop then persists STOPPED. Runtime.stop stops owned background processes, requests daemon shutdown, waits, then escalates through process-group SIGTERM/SIGKILL if necessary and waits again. This is implemented termination logic, not a runtime pass or proof that arbitrary Docker CC workloads are covered. A background kill may report permission_denied; callers must inspect outcomes. Resource limits are optional and require effective host support. Sandbox lifecycle/audit persistence is distinct from research continuity, consistent application checkpoints and independent backup.
Do not build a duplicate generic supervisor by default. First evaluate JiuwenBox as a reusable execution backend plus proxy, with narrow AI4R lifecycle adapters. Docker/OCI and the VM provider retain distinct responsibilities; do not force an extra bubblewrap layer around every CC without a demonstrated need.
